note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female with ~1-week history of dysuria, urinary frequency and suprapubic ache, with noted pink discoloration of urine today; clinician's impression: likely lower urinary tract infection (cystitis). Urine sample planned and antibiotics discussed.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Dysuria (burning/stinging with urination) for just under 1 week.
  - Increased urinary frequency interfering with university attendance.
  - Low suprapubic/“bottom of tummy” aching pain, worse with voiding.
  - Noted pink-tinged urine today (patient describes as “pink”; possibly blood).
- Timeline / progression:
  - Symptoms began a little under one week ago and have persisted; patient reports no improvement described.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Pain is worse during/when voiding.
  - No specific relieving factors documented.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - No fever reported.
  - No nausea or vomiting.
  - No flank/back pain.
  - No abnormal vaginal discharge reported.
  - Bowel habits: baseline irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) with variable stool consistency; no new bowel symptoms.
- Sexual and reproductive history:
  - Sexually active with a long-term boyfriend; typically no condom use.
  - Last unprotected intercourse approximately 1 week ago.
  - On combined oral contraceptive pill (type: combined).
  - Last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.
  - Pregnancy testing not documented / not performed during visit.
- Social / substance use:
  - Lives in university halls with a flatmate.
  - Drinks alcohol socially occasionally.
  - Tried cannabis (weed) for the first time approximately 1.5 weeks ago; patient concerned but clinician advised unlikely related to current symptoms.
  - Does not smoke cigarettes.
- Other relevant points:
  - Patient is a 19-year-old university student studying English.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
  - Takes a medication for IBS which “begins with an M” (exact name not documented).
- No other chronic medical conditions reported.
- Medications:
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill (dose/brand not documented).
  - IBS medication name incomplete (begins with "M"); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies:
  - Patient reports an adverse reaction to an antibiotic she names as “Clindamycin” (reaction details not specified).
  - Transcript contains potential conflict: clinician later noted “Ritib” when documenting allergy. (Conflict noted — see Quality checks.)

Social History:
- Living situation: university halls, lives with a flatmate.
- Education/employment: university student (English), started course a few months ago.
- Tobacco: does not smoke cigarettes.
- Alcohol: social drinking occasionally.
- Recreational drugs: tried cannabis once ~1.5 weeks ago; not a regular user.
- No financial or other lifestyle factors reported.

Family History:
- No family history of bladder or kidney problems reported.
- No other family medical history details provided.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- General / abdominal / GU exam: no physical examination performed during this consult; clinician stated they would not normally examine and was reassured by history.

Investigations:
- Urine sample: clinician requested a urine sample to be dropped off at practice for testing and for culture and sensitivity to be sent to the lab. No results yet.
- No imaging or laboratory results available in transcript.
- No pregnancy test documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis)
  - Assessment: Clinical impression of UTI/cystitis based on dysuria, frequency, suprapubic aching and appearance of pink urine today; no systemic features to suggest upper tract involvement.
  - Plan:
    - Obtain a urine sample today at the practice for urinalysis and urine culture/sensitivity.
    - Start empirical antibiotic therapy — clinician discussed options: Trimethoprim OR Nitrofurantoin (nitrofurantoin described as a three-day course). Exact antibiotic choice, dose, route, and frequency not documented in transcript.
    - If urine culture returns positive, adjust antibiotic based on sensitivities.
    - Advise adequate oral hydration.
    - Analgesia: paracetamol for pain as needed.
    - Safety-netting: return if symptoms worsen or do not improve within one week; seek prompt care for development of fever, flank/back pain, or vomiting (these were highlighted as concerning).
- Issue 2: Pink-tinged urine (possible hematuria)
  - Assessment: Noted pink urine today; to be evaluated with urinalysis and culture.
  - Plan:
    - Include in urine testing; manage as part of UTI workup.
    - Reassess based on test results and clinical course.
- Issue 3: Contraception / sexual activity / pregnancy risk
  - Assessment: On combined oral contraceptive pill; had unprotected sex ~1 week ago; last period 2 weeks ago.
  - Plan:
    - Clinician considered pregnancy as part of differential if symptoms persist; no pregnancy test documented. (No further action documented.)
- General plan items:
  - Arrange for patient to attend practice to drop off a urine sample; lab to process and clinician to relay results.
  - Advise avoidance of regular recreational cannabis use (counsel provided).
  - Follow-up: return to clinic in one week if no improvement, or sooner if red flag symptoms develop.
